1102.name: Sanhua
1102.synopsis:
1. Tip: Intro Skill, Resonance Skill, Resonance Liberation. This leaves behind [Ice Thorn], [Ice Prism], and [Glacier]. Hold Basic Attack, and release when the pointer hits the [Frostbite] zone to trigger [Ice Thorn], [Ice Prism], and [Glacier].
2. Rotation: E-R-H-Q.
3. Team Comp: The most suitable main DPS is Camellya. The team setup of Camellya + Sanhua + Shorekeeper/Verina/Baizhi works well. Please refer to the full guide for team rotation.
1102.rotationNotes:
1. Tip: Intro Skill, Resonance Skill, Resonance Liberation. This leaves behind [Ice Thorn], [Ice Prism], and [Glacier]. Hold Basic Attack, and release when the pointer hits the [Frostbite] zone to trigger [Ice Thorn], [Ice Prism], and [Glacier].
2. Rotation: E-R-H-Q.
3. Team Comp: The most suitable main DPS is Camellya. The team setup of Camellya + Sanhua + Shorekeeper/Verina/Baizhi works well. Please refer to the full guide for team rotation.

Skill Breakdown
1. Forte Circuit
When Basic Attack is held, a pointer moves across the energy bar. Release Basic Attack within the Forte Gauge [Frostbite] zone to unleash Heavy Attack Detonate (counts as Heavy Attack DMG).
● Heavy Attack Detonate detonates [Ice Thorn], [Ice Prism], and [Glacier] within range, dealing Glacio DMG (counts as Resonance Skill DMG).
● [Frostbite] Expansion: Each 1 stack of [Clarity] widens the [Frostbite] zone. Max 2 stacks.
● [Clarity] Gain: 5th Basic Attack hit, Intro Skill, Resonance Skill, Resonance Liberation. Using Heavy Attack Detonate consumes all [Clarity] stacks.
2. Resonance Liberation
Deal Glacio DMG, leave behind [Glacier].
3. Resonance Skill
Deal Glacio DMG, summon 1 [Ice Prism].
4. Normal Attack
● Basic Attack: up to 5-hit combo.
● Heavy Attack: Consumes STA to attack.
● Mid-air Attack: Consumes STA to perform a Plunging Attack.
● Dodge Counter: Triggered by dodging and shortly tapping Basic Attack.
5. Intro Skill
Deal Glacio DMG, leave behind 1 [Ice Thorn].
6. Outro Skill
Increase Basic Attack DMG of the next character.
Team Comp Analysis:
Sanhua’s Outro Skill increases the Basic Attack DMG of the next character, making her ideal for teams centered around Basic Attack main DPS.
Team Comp & Rotation:
In the following rotations: A = Basic Attack; H = Heavy Attack; E = Resonance Skill; R = Resonance Liberation; Q = Echo Skill.
● Cantarella + Sanhua + Shorekeeper/Verina/Baizhi
① Sanhua starts with ERH, not fully stacking Concerto Energy.
② Healer quickly fully charges Concerto Energy.
③ Sanhua re-enters with Intro Skill. Use EHQ to max out Concerto Energy.
④ Cantarella enters with Intro Skill. ERZ - Enhanced EQHE to achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out.
⑤ Repeat.
● Changli + Sanhua + Brant
Sanhua buffs Basic Attack DMG for Brant. Brant provides DPS, healing, and shielding, while boosting Changli’s Fusion and Resonance Skill DMG.
① Changli starts with EA, not fully stacking Concerto Energy.
② Sanhua ERHA to achieve full Concerto Energy.
③ Brant enters with Intro Skill, uses R-H-H, then enhanced E to achieve full Concerto Energy and leave the field.
④ Changli re-enters with Intro Skill, A-EA-EA, H (4 Enflamement stacks) + R + H (4 Enflamement stacks), achieve full Concerto Energy, swap out.
⑤ Repeat.
● Camellya + Sanhua + Shorekeeper/Verina/Baizhi
Sanhua increases Camellya's Basic Attack DMG, with the survival role offering healing or DMG bonus.
① Start with Camellya using E.
② Switch to Sanhua and use ERH without fully charging Concerto Energy.
③ Healer quickly fully charges Concerto Energy.
④ Bring in Camellya for Intro Skill. Use Basic Attack, but don’t max out Concerto Energy.
⑤ Switch to Sanhua EHQ to achieve full Concerto Energy;
⑥ Camellya re-enters with Intro Skill, uses Basic Attack fully charging Concerto Energy. Activates enhanced E + Basic Attack, fully charging Concerto Energy again. Leaves the field.

1105.name: Zhezhi
1105.synopsis:
Core Mechanics: [Afflatus] & [Phantasmic Imprint]
[Afflatus]: Max 90 points. Every 30 points summons one [Phantasmic Imprint] (up to 3) Cast [Resonance Skill - Manifestation]. Consumes 60 [Afflatus] to summon [Phantasmic Imprint - Left] and [Phantasmic Imprint - Right]. Casting [Heavy Attack - Conjuration] consumes 30 [Afflatus] to summon 1 [Phantasmic Imprint - Middle].
[Afflatus] Gain: Normal Attack/Intro Skill
[Phantasmic Imprint]: When a [Phantasmic Imprint] is present, Zhezhi's E is enhanced, consuming one [Phantasmic Imprint] to summon a Ivory Herald that deals DMG (considered Basic Attack DMG) while granting 1 stack of [Painter's Delight]. If a [Phantasmic Imprint] is present and [Painter's Delight] reaches 2 stacks, Zhezhi's E is further enhanced. Consumes all [Painter's Delight] stacks and all [Phantasmic Imprints] to summon a Ivory Herald that deals higher DMG (considered Basic Attack DMG) while increasing Zhezhi's Basic Attack DMG.
1105.rotationNotes:
Team Comp Analysis: Zhezhi provides Coordinated Attacks and boosts Glacio DMG and Resonance Skill DMG, making her a great fit for Glacio and Resonance Skill-based main DPS.

Rotation: A-A-A-E-H-E2-E2-E3-R-Q

1108.name: Hiyuki
1108.synopsis:
Hiyuki is a Glacio-Sword-wielding main DPS character. She utilizes the negative status, Glacio Chafe, in a unique way.
Most of Hiyuki's damage is considered Resonance Liberation Damage.
1108.rotationNotes:
Hiyuki will gain 1 stack of Snowforged Blade when outside of combat for 4 seconds, so it's best to wait 4 seconds before starting modes like Tower of Adversity.

Hiyuki is a character who utilizes Glacio Chafe throughout her kit. She has a unique passive that converts Glacio Chafe, into Glacio Bite, which is considered Glacio Chafe.
When Glacio Bite is inflicted, the target will take an instance of Glacio Bite DMG until the max stack is reached, which is 10. Hiyuki starts combat in Present Self State. When she uses her Basic Attack 3, she will gain 100 dedication, maxing out at 300. When she cast her Resonance Skill, she will gain an additional 100 dedication. Once her forte is maxed, she will be able to cast Forclaimed Self by using her Resonance Liberation.
Once she is in the Forclaimed Self state, her Forte Bar changes. Casting Basic Attacks will fill up her Forte. Her Resonance Skill will now be upgraded, putting Hiyuki in the air to follow up with Basic Attacks. When her Forte is 1/3 full, she is able to cast Iai when you Dodge, followed up with Basic Attack. Each cast of Iai is cast, Hiyuki will gain one stack of Whiteout Bitterfrost.
Once she has 3 stacks, she is able to cast her enhanced Forte with a Heavy Attack, Bitterfrost: Foreclaimed Self, dealing significant Resonance Liberation Damage. She will also gain one stack of Snowforged Blade. Hiyuki can hold 3 stacks of Snowforged Blade, and each stack will power up Hiyuki's Enhanced Resonance Liberation.
She also gains 1 stack when she is out of combat for more than 4 seconds. When you hold down the Resonance Liberation, she will consume each stack of Snowforged Blade to increase the damage of her Resonance Liberation. Hiyuki's Outro Skill will amplify Glacio damage that hits targets affected by Glacio Chafe.

1109.name: Lucilla
1109.synopsis:
Lucilla is a Glacio, Rectifier sub-DPS character who specializes in supporting two gameplay styles depending on her Resonance Mode. Glacio Chafe and Echo.
She deals primarily Basic Attack damage, or Echo Skill DMG.
She holds 0 Resonance Energy, and her Resonance Liberation is unlocked upon filling her Forte Bar.
1109.rotationNotes:
Use Resonance Skill and Basic Attack to bring up the Focus Ring cursor → Land inside Perfect Focus → Restore Trace → Reach 3 Photos / full Forte Bar → Cast Resonance Liberation → Use Basic Attack chain until Tracing Forms Stage 3 → Hold or press Basic Attack to consume Photos → Cast Letting It Go → Use Outro Skill

Lucilla has two gameplay styles. Glacio Chafe support, and Echo support. Her gameplay loop is the same with each mode, but her buffs are different.
Lucilla's Resonance Skill will Pull nearby targets and bring up a cursor. After casting Resonance Skill or Basic Attack 3, hold Basic Attack or Resonance Skill to deploy Lucilla’s Focus Ring. You will hold this down until the Focus Ring Cursor is full, to deal additional damage, and restore Trace. 
Every 50 Trace will generate one Photo for Lucilla. Each Photo is 1/3 of her Forte Bar, maxing out at 3. Landing the cursor inside Perfect Focus strengthens the Focus Ring effect, so this should be your goal every time.
When Lucilla has 3 Photos, maxing out her Forte bar, Her Resonance Liberation will unlock. When casting her Resonance Liberation Lucilla will deal Glacio Damage and enter Reminiscence.
Lucilla gains enhancements depending on her Resonance Mode.
Glacio Chafe: 
Grants Lucilla 30% Basic Attack DMG Bonus for 10 seconds, and she will gain 4 stacks of Film Roll for 30 seconds, and whenever another team member inflicts Glacio Chafe, Lucilla will consume 1 stack of Film Roll and inflict Glacio Chafe on two nearby targets.
Echo:
Lucilla gains 30% Echo Skill DMG Bonus for 10 seconds, and she will gain 1 stack of Zoom, increasing the Crit DMG of the active Resonator's Echo Skill by 10%. Each effect lasts 30 seconds.
When casting Basic Attack 3 while in Reminiscence, Lucilla can continuously attack the target by holding or pressing Normal Attack to consume Photo Stack. Each Photo Consumed will deal damage and inflict Glacio Chafe if in Glacio Chafe Resonance Mode, and while in Echo Resonance Mode each Photo Stack will count as a separate Echo Skill used. When all stacks are consumed, she will automatically perform Letting It Go. Lucilla is immune to interruptions and damage when casting Letting It Go. Casting Letting It Go ends her Resonance Liberation Mode.
Lucilla's Outro Skill changes depending on Resonance Mode. 
Glacio Chafe: Glacio Chafe DMG against targets are amplified by 60% for 30 Seconds. 
Echo: Grants 50% Echo Skill DMG Amplification to the incoming Resonator for 14 seconds. This effect ends when that Resonator is switched off.

1203.name: Encore
1203.synopsis:
Core Mechanics: [Mayhem]. When [Mayhem] is full, using a Heavy Attack consumes all [Mayhem] and triggers a Mayhem state. While in this state, Encore takes 70% less DMG, and switching characters won’t cancel the effect. When it ends, she deals Fusion DMG.
While under Resonance Liberation, if Encore fills the [Mayhem] again, a Heavy Attack will trigger Cosmos' Mayhem state. This state also reduces DMG taken by 70% and persists through character switches. When it ends, she unleashes Cosmos Rupture for Fusion DMG.
[Mayhem] Gain: Hitting enemies with Normal Attack, Resonance Skill, or Intro Skill restores [Mayhem]. Under Resonance Liberation, all hits restore [Mayhem].
Rotation: E1→E2→R→AAAA*n→H.

1204.synopsis:

[Annoyance] Gain: Basic Attack/Intro Skill/Resonance Skill.

1206.name: Brant
1206.synopsis:
Team compositions: The most common team for Brant is a free to play friendly team featuring Sanhua to provide basic attack damage amplification which significantly boosts his forte skill. You can also pai him with Changli since Brant’s outro skill synergises really well with Changli
Output suggestions: For Brant to work in any team composition, you simply need to use his liberation, hold basic attack to use his heavy attack twice and then proceed to spam your basic attacks in mid air which will fully fill his Bravo stacks. From there, all you need to do is to press your skill to drop the anchor on the enemy to deal massive damage 
Basic operations include: Ult→HA1→HA2→BA3->BA4→Skill
BA=Basic Attack, Ult=Liberation HA= Heavy attack
1206.rotationNotes:
If you’re into characters that are very fun to play, does decent damage, provides some of the the best buffing and sustaining capabilities in the game and have free to play weapons and teams readily available, then Brant is the right character for you.

Brant’s kit is heavily focused on his mid air basic attacks so knowing how they work in different situations will make him even more enjoyable. Whenever you finish BA1,BA2,or BA3 in mid air, he will perform a flip shot. When the flip shot ends, it means you can dodge in mid air. This means that Brant is not vulnerable in mid air compared to most characters because every basic attack in mid air except BA4 resets your dodge attempts. Whenever your dodge attempts resets, it means you can proceed with the next stage of his basic attack. 
Brant has access to heavy attacks as well and here’s how they work. You need to go in mid air by jumping or using his skill and then hold your basic attack button to start the Basic attack stage 1 and follow up with the first heavy attack. Now keep holding it and he will follow up with the second heavy attack. From there you can spam basic attacks to use basic attack 3 and 4. Keep in mind that if you press basic attack instead to use stage 1, it means you have exhausted the chance to use the heavy attack stage 1 after the flip shot is completed. Holding it afterwards will start heavy attack stage 2 but continuously pressing basic attacks will proceed with stage 2,3 and 4.
This detail is very important because during an intro skill, Brant does basic stage 1 and ends with a flip shot which means that holding your basic attack button afterwards will perform heavy attack stage 2 from there so be sure to keep that in mind. And that’s all you need to know on how to play Brant.
More detailed rotation for Brant’s strongest team with Changli and Lupa is as follows:
Changli skill→Ult (keep holding BA) → HA→BA→Skill→BA→Echo Skill→swap to lupa→skill 2x→Ult→BA 5x →skill→Brant intro→Ult→Hold BA→HA2→BA3→BA4→Skill→echo skill→Changli intro
BA=Basic Attack, Ult=Liberation HA= Heavy attack

1207.name: Lupa
1207.synopsis:
1. Tip: After casting Resonance Liberation, use [Foebreaker] to trigger [Burning Matchpoint]. Within 12 seconds, perform full Basic Attacks to max [Wolflame], then use [Wolf's Gnawing], [Wolf's Claw], and finish with [Dance With the Wolf: Climax].
2. Rotation: Lupa R-A/E-A*n-H-A- Ultimate E.
3. Team Comp: The most suitable ally is Changli and Brant. The team setup of Changli + Lupa + Brant works well. Please refer to the full guide for team rotation.
1207.rotationNotes:
Skill Breakdown
1. Normal Attack
      ● Basic Attack: 4-hit combo. After A3, can follow up with the 1st hit of Mid-air Attack. After Dodge Counter / Starfall / Shewolf's Hunt / Feral Fang, can chain into A2.
      ● Heavy Attack: Consumes STA to attack.
      ● Heavy Attack - Wolf's Gnawing: Requires 50 [Wolflame].
      ● Heavy Attack - Wolf's Claw: Requires 50 [Wolflame] + 1 [Wolfaith]. Can be shortcut-cast after Firestrike / Wolf's Gnawing.
      ● Mid-air Attack: 3-hit combo.
      ● Mid-air Attack - Firestrike: Replaces 3rd hit of Mid-air Attack if [Wolflame] ≥ 50 (counts as Heavy Attack DMG).
      ● Plunging Attack - Hold Basic Attack mid-air to cast, then short tap Basic Attack for Starfall.
      ● Basic Attack - Starfall: Deals Fusion DMG.
      ● Dodge Counter: Triggers Basic Attack on a successful dodge.
2. Resonance Skill
      ● Shewolf's Hunt (E1): Restores 15 [Wolflame], marks enemy for 8s, can follow up with Feral Fang. Hold to leap.
      ● Feral Fang (E2): Restores 15 [Wolflame], deals increased DMG to marked enemies.
      ● Inherent Skill: Lupa killing a marked enemy resets Shewolf's Hunt CD.
3. Forte Circuit
      ● Wildfire Banner: Boosts Lupa's ATK for 8s during certain skills.
      ● Resonance Skill - Dance With the Wolf (Enhanced E): Requires 2 [Wolfaith], counts as Resonance Liberation DMG.
      ● Resonance Skill - Dance With the Wolf: Climax (Ultimate E): Requires 2 [Wolfaith] + Burning Matchpoint. Also counts as Resonance Liberation DMG.
      ● Resonance Skill - Set the Arena Ablaze (Coordinated E): Within 8 seconds after casting enhanced/Ultimate E, switching characters lets the next teammate trigger a Lupa's Coordinated Attack 1 time when they use Resonance Liberation (counts as Resonance Skill DMG).
      ● [Wolflame] Gain: Up to 100 points. Gained via Normal Attack, Resonance Skill, Resonance Liberation.
      ● [Wolfaith] Gain: Up to 2 points. Lasts 10s. The duration is reset when Wolfaith is restored. At the end of its duration, each remaining point of [Wolfaith] becomes 50 points of [Wolflame]. Restore 1 point when casting Wolf's Gnawing / Wolf's Claw / Firestrike.
4. Resonance Liberation
      Deals DMG, clears [Wolfaith], restores 100 [Wolflame]. Short press Basic Attack or Resonance Skill to trigger Resonance Skill - Foebreaker.
      ● Resonance Skill - Foebreaker: Consumes all [Wolflame], deals DMG, enters Burning Matchpoint.
      ● Burning Matchpoint: 12s duration. Greatly boosts [Wolflame] gain from Normal Attack. Shewolf's Hunt/Feral Fang is unavailable.
      After activating Resonance Liberation, for 35 seconds your entire team can trigger up to 3 recovery effects and gain Pack Hunt and Glory (Glory requires unlocking an Inherent Skill).
      ● Pack Hunt: Increases ATK by 6%. When attacking a boss, Fusion DMG is increased by 10%. If there are 3 Fusion characters on the team, Fusion DMG gets an additional 10% boost. Using an Intro Skill grants an additional 6% ATK, stacking up to 18%. Once Pack Hunt is maxed, triggers Wild Hunt, which can only activate once per instance of Pack Hunt.
      ● Glory: Ignores 3% of enemy Fusion RES. For each additional Fusion character besides Lupa, this bonus increases by 3%, up to 9%. With 3 Fusion characters in the team, gain an extra 6%.
5. Intro Skill
      ● Deals Fusion DMG to the target. Allows a follow-up with the 3rd hit of Lupa's Mid-air Attack by tapping Basic Attack shortly after.
      ● Enhanced Intro Skill: When in Wild Hunt, Lupa's Intro Skill changes. Consumes all Pack Hunt and Glory on the team to deal powerful Fusion DMG (counts as Resonance Liberation DMG).
6. Outro Skill
        Boosts the next character's Fusion DMG and Basic Attack DMG.
Team Comp Analysis:
Lupa fits exclusively into Fusion teams. She mainly contributes through Resonance Liberation DMG and Outro Skill can boost allies' Fusion and Basic Attack DMG. Ideal teammates are Changli and Brant.
Team Comp & Rotation:
In the following rotations: A = Basic Attack; H = Heavy Attack; E = Resonance Skill; R = Resonance Liberation; Q = Echo Skill.
● Changli + Lupa + Brant.
The best team. Triple core synergy. Changli boosts Lupa's Fusion DMG and Resonance Liberation DMG. Lupa boosts Brant's Fusion and Basic Attack DMG. Brant boosts Changli's Fusion and Resonance Skill DMG, and provides teamwide healing.
① Changli starts with EA - EA, not fully stacking Concerto Energy;
② Lupa R-A/E-A*n-H-A- Ultimate E. Achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
③ Brant enters with Intro Skill, uses R-H-H, then enhanced E to achieve full Concerto Energy and leave the field.
④ Changli takes the field with Intro Skill + A-EA-H-R-H. Achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
⑤ Lupa enters with enhanced Intro Skill. Repeat.
● Encore + Lupa + Brant.
Lupa buffs Encore's Fusion DMG and Basic Attack DMG. Brant supports Lupa with Fusion and Resonance Skill DMG, plus team healing.
① Encore starts with E;
② Lupa R-A/E-A*n-H-A- Ultimate E. Achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
③ Encore takes the field with Intro Skill + R-E1E2-4A*3-H. Achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
④ Brant enters with Intro Skill, uses R-H-H, then enhanced E to achieve full Concerto Energy and leave the field;
⑤ Lupa enters with enhanced Intro Skill. Repeat.
● Chixia + Lupa + Brant.
Lupa buffs Brant's Fusion DMG and Basic Attack DMG. Brant boosts Chixia's Fusion and Resonance Skill DMG, and heals the team.
① Chixia starts with EE, not fully stacking Concerto Energy;
② Lupa R-A/E-A*n-H-A- Ultimate E. Achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
③ Brant enters with Intro Skill, uses R-H-H, then enhanced E to achieve full Concerto Energy and leave the field.
④ Chixia enters with Intro Skill + Held E-A-R- Held E-A- Held E-A to achieve full Concerto Energy and swap out;
⑤ Lupa enters with enhanced Intro Skill. Repeat.

2. Rotation: Lupa R-A/E-A*n-H-A- Ultimate E.

1208.name: Galbrena
1208.synopsis:
Its important to use as many Echo skills with Galbrena to enhance her most powerful state, Demon Hypostasis.
Pairing her with specific allies is highly recommended as they fuel her damage. Always start your rotation with her Resonance Liberation.
1208.rotationNotes:
Galbrena is a fusion pistol wielding character that specializes in high spurts of damage, and utilizes your teams Echo Skills to power up her enhanced Resonance Skill.

Galbrena specializes in Echo Skill Damage, and Heavy Attack Damage, but most of her damage comes from Echo skill damage, which most of her kit is considered.
When paired with Echo Skill users, she can output crazy damage, but she also has other teams that work exceptionally well. 
For each unique echo used in the party used, the damage of her attacks in the Demon Hypostasis Mode greatly increases.
She pairs exceptionally well with characters who use unique echo skills in their kit. 
Her gameplay consist of using other characters unique echo skills to power up her "Demon Hypostasis Mode", and then utilizing any part of her kit to build up her forte, and then activating the Demon Hypostasis mode with her Enhanced Resonance Skill.
In this state, all of her attacks are enhanced, and using her basic attack combo will unleash incredible damage. Each attack will use her built up gauge, and when its depleted, the Demon Hypostasis mode will end.
Additionally, her Resonance Liberation increases the Multiplier of her Demon Hypostasis mode.

1209.name: Mornye
1209.synopsis:
Mornye is a powerful support resonator who can heal allies, and when played with other Tune Rupture Units, she can provide insane buffs to the entire teams damage.
She functions as a flexible 3rd option in many teams, but does very well when paired with characters like Lynae, who can perform a Tune Rupture.
1209.rotationNotes:
Mornye scales with Def, so be careful with what echoes you equip her with.
Mornye needs 260% Energy Regen to max out her buffs. Very powerful all around character who can fit into virtually any team.

Mornye is is a fusion broadblade character who specalizes in healing, buffing allies, and increases the damage that enemies receive from all allies.
She provides a buff that also increases the Off-Tune Buildup Rate, allowing more ease with performing Tune Breaks.
Additionally, any enemy affected by Tune Rupture - Interfered, will take increased damage based on the amount of Energy Regen Mornye has.
Mornye's rotation consist of her filling up her initial forte gauge, Rest Mass Energy, by using any of her attacks, and then using her Heavy Attack to enter Wide Field Observation Mode, which generates Syntony Field. Syntony Field provides the following buffs: Continous Healing, Increased Off-Tune Buildup Rate, and enhanced interruption resistance for 25 seconds.
When Mornye cast her Resonance Liberation while in the Syntony Field, she will upgrade her Syntony Field to High Syntony Field, which further increases the teams DEF.
When Mornye fills up her Forte Gauge while in Wide FIeld Observation Mode, she can cast her Heavy Attack to unleash a powerful attack that marks the enemy with Observation Marker.
When Enemies with the marker are affected by Tune Break, this marker upgrades to an Interfered Marker.
Finally, when an enemy with this marker is affected by a Tune Rupture - Interfered, they will be debuffed, and take increased damage by the entire team. Mornye also has a powerful Outro Skill, which Amplifies the entire teams Attribute Damage.

1210.name: Aemeath
1210.synopsis: Aemeath is a Fusion, Sword Wielding Main Damage Dealer who utilizes Off-Tune effects to enhance her kit, and deals insane AoE Damage. She is capable of swapping and jointly attacking the enemy with her Mech, and then finishing them off with her incredible Rail Gun. She utilizes Resonance Liberation DMG to deal damage.
1210.rotationNotes:
Use Aemeath's initial Resonance Liberation ONLY after an intro skill.
This will allow her to gain 2 stacks of her Response Rate when her Resonance Liberation is used.
Be sure that Aemeath has all buffs before unleashing her Finale finisher, as it is a huge portion of her overall damage.

Resonance Rate is Capped at 4, and as Aemeath raises her Forge Gauge by performing attacks, she unlocks the ability is able to cast her Enhanced Resonance Skill, Seraphic Duo.
Seraphic Duo is only castable after performing Basic Attack 4 in either Mech or Human form, and casting it depletes her forte.
The Enhanced Resonance Skill will grant Aemeath one stack of Response Rate. Casting Aemeath's Resonance Liberation will also grant one stack of Response Rate, and unlock the ability to cast her Enhanced Resonance Liberation.
If Aemeath performs an Intro Skill, her Resonance Liberation will give two stacks of Response Rate instead. Once she reaches 4 stacks, she enters a new state, enhancing her Resonance Skills.

Unleashing this powerful attack deals a gigantic nuke of AoE fusion damage to every enemy present.

1. Forte Circuit
Normal Attack and Resonance Skill are replaced by Fleurdelys-form skills, all of which generate [Conviction], up to 120 points.
2. Resonance Liberation
Switches to Fleurdelys form, consumes HP, and enters [Manifest] state. Fleurdelys's A5, 2nd hit of Mid-air Attack, and E2 instantly trigger [Aero Erosion] 1 time (consumes [Aero Erosion] stacks).
When Fleurdelys is in [Manifest] state and holds different [Sword Shadows], various effects are triggered.
● Purple Sword + [Manifest]: Increases Fleurdelys' resistance to interruption. A4 summons a force field that slows enemies within range.
● Green Sword + [Manifest]: Reduces the interval between [Aero Erosion] trigger and increases [Aero Erosion] DMG.
● Blue Sword + [Manifest]: After using E2 and dealing DMG, Fleurdelys' A5, 2nd hit of Mid-air Attack, and enhanced Heavy Attack will spread the highest Aero Negative Status stack from a target to all enemies within the area.
Fleurdelys generates [Conviction] upon hitting enemies.
At 120 [Conviction], tapping Resonance Liberation casts R2. The casting consumes all [Conviction], removes [Manifest], restores HP, and deals Aero DMG. The DMG scales with the target's Aero Negative Status stacks (up to 5 stacks) and clears the Aero Negative Status stacks afterward.

Deals Aero DMG (counts as Basic Attack DMG), applies 2 stacks of Aero Negative Status, and summons [Sword of Virtue's Shadow] (Purple).

1506.name: Phoebe
1506.synopsis: Core Mechanic: Forte Circuit Phoebe can switch states by maxing out [Prayer]. When [Prayer] is full, her Basic Attack and Resonance Skill icons glow. Skill Breakdown
1. Forte Circuit
     With Zani in the team, whenever an allied unit applies [Spectro Frazzle] to an enemy, it immediately triggers DMG and converts the stacks into equal amount of [Heliacal Ember] (up to 60 stacks), enabling the set bonus from [Eternal Radiance]. At the same time, Zani gains Forte Gauge [Blaze].
     While in the Inferno Mode, Zani unlocks Heavy Slash skills, treated as both Heavy Attack DMG and [Spectro Frazzle] DMG. Using these skills will consume [Blaze].
     ● [Blaze]: Up to 100 outside Inferno Mode. Up to 150 during Inferno Mode. Cast Targeted Action/Forcible Riposte to obtain 10 points. 5 points per stack when [Spectro Frazzle] converts into [Heliacal Ember]. 50 points upon using Resonance Liberation - Rekindle.
     ● [Redundant Energy]: Max cap is 100. Gain: Hit with Basic Attack/Intro Skill/Pinpoint Strike. Cast standard Resonance Skill. Cannot gain [Redundant Energy] while in Inferno Mode.
2. Resonance Liberation
     Deals Spectro DMG and enters Inferno Mode.
     ● Inferno Mode: Basic Attack multiplier increases. When [Blaze] drops below 30 or Inferno Mode lasts for 8 seconds, the Resonance Liberation will upgrade to an enhanced version. Casting the enhanced version exits Inferno Mode.
3. Resonance Skill
     ● Standard Defense Protocol: Attack and enter block state. Afterward, press Basic Attack briefly to chain into the 3rd hit, capable of stagnating enemies. Taking DMG during the block reduces incoming DMG, stagnates nearby enemies, triggers a Pinpoint Strike.
     ● Crisis Response Protocol: Available when [Redundant Energy] is full and Zani is not in Inferno Mode. Performed by holding the Resonance Skill to block. During the block, releasing the skill or when the duration ends, she will consume all [Redundant Energy] to perform Targeted Action. If attacked during the block, Zani will reduce DMG, stagnate nearby enemies, and consume all [Redundant Energy] to perform Forcible Riposte.
4. Normal Attack
     ● Basic Attack: 4-hit combo + one [Breakthrough]. A1-A2-A3-A (Breakthrough) - A4. In Inferno Mode, A3 can stagnate enemies.
     ● Heavy Attack: Consumes STA to deal Spectro DMG, followed by 3rd hit of Basic Attack.
     ● Mid-air Attack: Consumes STA to perform a Plunging Attack, followed by 3rd hit of Basic Attack.
     ● Dodge Counter: After a successful dodge, perform a Basic Attack, followed by 3rd hit of Basic Attack.
5. Intro Skill
     Attacks the target, dealing Spectro DMG.
6. Outro Skill
     Attacks the target, dealing Spectro DMG. All [Heliacal Ember] stacks are cleared, and the DMG is increased based on the number of [Heliacal Ember] stacks (considered as Spectro Frazzle DMG). Teammates deal increased Spectro DMG for 20 seconds to enemies with [Heliacal Ember].

1508.synopsis: Chisa is a Havoc Broadblade user who specializes in inflicting Havoc Bane, and enhancing the team's Negative Status infliction and damage. Her gameplay consists of inflicting the Unseen Snare buff, to allow all party members who inflict or deal Negative Status damage to ignore the enemy's defense. She is also able to heal thanks to her liberation, making her a great unit to buff the party.

Chisa can use ATK echoes to provide more healing, while offering competetive damage. It's important to use her liberation before she begins to attack, as it amplifies all of her Sawring DMG.
You can hold Chisa's enhanced Resonance Skill to additionally pull in enemies and deal a bit of damage. Chisa can hover and move midair on her scissors, which is pretty cool...

Chisa is a character who will be a great asset to team's who inflict Negative Statuses. Not only is she able to fully buff the team, heal, and deal damage, but she is also able to fully stack and utilize Havoc Bane, another Negative Status, on her own. Havoc Bane decreases the target's defense by 2% per stack up to 6 stacks(12%), additionally.
 Chisa can inflict "Unseen Snare" on enemies via multiple methods. When the target marked by Unseen Snare is hit, Chisa will inflict 1 stack of Havoc Bane onto them. Chisa's Outro Skill grants a significant buff to the team. She increases the max stack of every Negative Status by 3 for 15 seconds, and every party member who inflicts or deals Negative Status DMG will be granted "Thread of Bane" which allows the user to ignore 18% of the target's defense.
Chisa excels at buffing the party and allowing the entire team to ignore enemy defense, while also stacking their Negative Status, regardless of the type.

1509.name: Lynae
1509.synopsis: Lynae is a Spectro Gun Wielding character who specializes in SubDPS damage, and utilizing her Tune Shifting abilities, while also buffing her incoming allies. She utilizes in Basic Attack DMG to deal damage.
1509.rotationNotes:
Lyane is a great Sub-DPS damage dealer, and can buff Resonance Liberation damage users.
She has fast forte generation, and doesn't need to be on field for long.
She offers a ton of buffs, and its important to activate each of her buffs during her rotation.

Lynae has two states, Default State, and Roller Skating Mode. Lynae also has a couple of unique energy mechanic with her forte, called Overflow, and Lumiflow. Overflow is used in default state, and Lumiflow is used in Roller Skating state.
In her default state, Lynae can use a heavy attack to charge up her energy, and releasing it causes her to dash forward, deal damage, and enter into Roller Skater Mode. In Roller Skater mode, she can hold down the normal attack to spam basic attacks while gliding around the enemy, which builds up Lumiflow.
At max Lumiflow, Lynae can cast Polychrome Leap, which will use 1/3 of her Lumiflow per jump, maxing out at 3. Each Jump will grant Lynae a stack of True Color, and when she reached max stacks, she can follow up her Polychrome Leap with her Enhanced Roller Skate Plunge Attack, which grants a Tune Break Boost to all allies, and inflicts either of the Tune Shifting effects on the enemy. 
Finally, her outro skill Amplifies Liberation and All Type DMG of for the incoming character.

1510.name: Luuk Herssen
1510.synopsis:
Luuk is a spectro gauntlet character who acts as a premier Tune Strain Interfered main damage dealer.
His entire kit is considered Basic Attack Damage.
He gains his forte from his teammates outro skills, and powers up his Resonance Liberation significantly by utilizing his Enhanced Resonance Skill.
1510.rotationNotes:
Always cast Luuks Resonance Liberation after utilizing his full Forte Circuit and Enhanced Resonance Skills for the most damage output.
Golden Reflux can be used to immediately gain a stack of Tune Strain - Interfered. It can be used in Mid-Air by casting Luuks Resonance Skill. Luuk can cast a Heavy Attack to jump into the air, dealing Spectro DMG.

Luuk gains his Forte, Ichor Flow, when Normal Attack and Resonance Skill hit the target. Additionally, when any of Luuks teammates trigger their outro skills and swap to Luuk, he will gain 200 Ichor Flow. Upon casting Intro Skill, Luuk will gains 100 Ichor Flow. Ichor Flow caps at 300, and allow 3 cast of his Enhanced Resonance Skills.
When his Forte is filled, Luuk enters Aureate Judge State, allowing him to cast one of three Enhanced Resonance Skills. The Enhanced Resonance Skill becomes available after Basic Attack 4, or Aerial Basic Attack 3. Upon casting the Enhanced Resonance Skill 3 times, Luuk can follow up with an aerial slam to detonate the final Ichor Attack.
Each of these Resonance Skill cast grants Luuk a stack of Endnote on the Endgame, and each stack increases the damage multiplier of Luuks Resonance Liberation by 25%, up to 75%. It is very important to use Luuk's Forte Circuit and Enhanced Resonance Skills before casting his Resonance Liberation as a finisher.
Finally, Luuk's Outro Skill is a powerful attack, dealing significant Spectro Dmg.
Luuk triggers Tune Strain - Interfered by many methods. By inflicting and responding to Tune Strain - Interfered, Luuk Herssen deals more Total DMG.
By utilizing the Tune Break Boost provided by other Resonators in the team, Luuk Herssen gains substantial DMG Amplification.

      Deals Havoc DMG and enables Basic Attacks to directly trigger the third hit for a short duration. While in [Mirage], triggers Coordinated Attacks 3 times.
      Paired with her Forte Circuit, using Intro Skill restores Concerto Energy when an ally performs an Echo Skill. Since most of Cantarella’s skills count as Echo Skills, she fully benefits from this effect, enabling rapid Concerto Energy regeneration.
6. Outro Skill
      Boosts the next character's Havoc DMG and Resonance Skill DMG.

1. Tip: In normal state, quickly build up passive. Enter enhanced state, then hold Basic Attack to consume passive and unleash her finishing strike [Perception Drain].
2. Rotation: Intro Skill + ERH-EQAAAE + Outro Skill.
3. Team Comp: Cantarella currently fits best as a sub-DPS in a Jinhsi team. The team setup of Jinhsi + Cantarella + Verina/Shorekeeper works well. Please refer to the full guide for team rotation.

1608.name: Phrolova

1. Tip: Use A3 or E to gain [Volatile Note] and enter [Reincarnate]. Follow up with enhanced A or E to build [Volatile Note]. Once at 6 stacks of [Volatile Note], cast enhanced H and activate Resonance Liberation before swapping out. Rotation: 3A - Enhanced A/E - E - Enhanced A/E - Q - 3A - Enhanced A/E - Enhanced H - R - Outro Skill + swap out.

1110.name: Suisui
1110.synopsis:
Suisui is a 5-Star, Glacio, Rectifier Resonator who functions primarily as a healer and team-wide support. 
She excels are providing support and buffs to characters who inflict negative statuses.
1110.rotationNotes:
Build Cloud Breath → enter Drizzle Stance → build Floral Epistle → cast Liberation → Outro at 600 Floral Epistle whenever possible.

Suisui’s kit revolves around switching between two stances, building Cloud Breath in Zephyr Stance before entering Drizzle Stance and generating Floral Epistle.
She begins combat in Zephyr Stance. During this stance, her Basic Attacks, Dodge Counters, Resonance Skill, and successful dodges build Cloud Breath.
Once her Cloud Breath reaches its maximum of 120, she can cast Awakening Spring to consume all Cloud Breath, pull nearby enemies together, inflict Glacio Chafe, and enter Drizzle Stance. Her Intro Skill can also immediately consume her Cloud Breath and place her into Drizzle Stance.
While in Drizzle Stance, Suisui will start to build Floral Epistle through her attacks, Resonance Skill, and successful dodges. Her Resonance Skill restores 100 Floral Epistle, while a successful dodge using Parting Mist restores 100.
Her Resonance Liberation creates Ceaseless Landscape for 30 seconds. While it is active, teammates can increase the maximum stacks of certain Negative Status effects:
Spectro Frazzle, Fusion Burst, Glacio Chafe, and Aero Erosion gain one additional maximum stack.
Electro Flare and Electro Rage gain up to three additional maximum stacks.
Consuming Havoc Bane allows Havoc damage to ignore 6% of the target’s DEF.
Suisui’s Outro Skill, Rippling Waters, consumes all her Floral Epistle and grants the team 25% All DMG Amplification for 30 seconds, and granting Suisui Plume Steps.
Plume steps grants Reflecting Shadows to all resonators for 6 seconds, inflicts one stack of Glacio Chafe on all enemies within Suisui’s Resonance Liberation domain, and provides healing to active resonators.
The amount consumed determines how many Plume Steps she performs during Roaming Transcendent:
0 Floral Epistle: Grants Reflecting Shadows, increasing interruption resistance.
200 Floral Epistle: Unlocks the first Plume Step.
400 Floral Epistle: Unlocks the second Plume Step and provides additional damage scaling based on Suisui’s Energy Regen above 200%, up to 12%.
600 Floral Epistle: Unlocks the third Plume Step and grants Undulating Mist after the first Plume Step.
Undulating Mist provides an ATK increase whenever the active Resonator consumes Negative Status or Electro Rage stacks. The bonus scales with Suisui’s Energy Regen above 200% and can provide up to 50% ATK.

1309.name: Rover: Electro
1309.synopsis: Electro Rover is an Electro, Sword DPS or support character who can utilize multiple elements as a main DPS, or support negative status teams with a powerful outro buff.
1309.rotationNotes:
Electro Rover is great in negative status teams. A simple support rotation is as follows. Swap into Rover with Intro Skill, use Resonance Skill, follow with Basic Attacks to fill Electric Surge, press Overshock for the team ATK buff, then Outro into your main DPS to trigger Electro Core.
A simple DPS rotation is: swap into Rover with Intro Skill, use Resonance Skill, build Electric Surge, hold Overshock to enter Apex Resonance, then use Thrum of All Sounds combos as your main damage window before swapping out.

Electro Rover is an Electro character who can work as either a buffer for negative statuses or an on-field DPS. Their main mechanic is Electric Surge, which is built through Intro Skill, Basic Attacks, and Resonance Skill. Once Electric Surge is full, Rover's Skill becomes Overshock.
Pressing Overshock spends Electric Surge to give the whole team a 10% ATK Bonus for 20 seconds, making this the faster support option. Holding Overshock instead spends the gauge and 60 Concerto Energy to enter Apex Resonance, unlocking Thrum of All Sounds, Rover's main damage mode.
In Apex Resonance, Rover consumes Thunder Rage over time and uses Thrum of All Sounds to chain multi-element attacks. These attacks can deal Spectro, Havoc, Aero, and Electro-related damage through Thunder Bane, so Electro Rover is not a pure Electro-only DPS. Their kit is built around swapping between quick team utility and a longer personal damage window.
Electro Rover also has a parry mechanic. Holding Basic Attack enters Parry Stance, reducing damage taken and preventing interruption. Releasing it performs Riposte Strike, and timing it against an enemy attack lets Rover negate the hit, Stagnate enemies, and follow up with Riposte Strike: Crumble. This gives them extra skill expression, especially when played on-field.
Their Outro gives the incoming character Electro Core. When that character inflicts a Negative Status, Electro Core is consumed to grant 25% All DMG Amplification for 14 seconds. Because of this, Electro Rover should work best with characters who can reliably trigger Negative Statuses during their damage window.

1610.name: Yangyang: Xuanling
1610.synopsis: Yangyang is a Havoc, sword main DPS character who utilizes Havoc Bane to provide buffs to herself, dealing primarily Heavy Attack damage.
1610.rotationNotes:
Yangyang can use her Intro Skill to gain one Azure Plume, and then use her Resonance Liberation to gain another Azure Plume to immediately use her Enhanced Heavy Attack.
Support setup → Yangyang Intro → Resonance Liberation → Enhanced Heavy Attack → Basic Attacks until Melody is empty → Sword Stance Flow → Basic Attacks until Melody is empty → Sword Stance Flow → Enhanced Heavy Attack sequence.

Yangyang: Xuanling is a Havoc damage dealer who focuses heavily on Heavy Attack DMG. She swaps between two sword stances, builds Azure Plume, applies Havoc Bane, and then spends those resources on powerful Heavy Attacks.
She has two main stances: Azure Sword Stance and Feather Sword Stance. While using her Basic Attacks, she consumes Melody. Once her Melody is empty, her Resonance Skill changes into Sword Stance Flow, which swaps her into the opposite stance, restores her Melody back to full, and gives her 1 Azure Plume.
Azure Plume is the most important part of her rotation. She can hold up to 2 Azure Plume, and once she reaches 2, she unlocks her enhanced Heavy Attack. Depending on which stance she is in, the Heavy Attack changes.
In Azure Sword Stance, her Heavy Attack creates a large cyclone in front of her. This is a big burst hit and is considered Heavy Attack DMG.
In Feather Sword Stance, her Heavy Attack leads into Feather Fall, which then gives her access to Havoc in Bloom. During this state, her Basic Attacks are replaced with a short Heavy Attack combo.
Xuanling applies Havoc Bane through her Intro, Basic Attack Stage 4, Heavy Attacks, Liberation, and some of her follow-up effects. Havoc Bane increases the damage she deals to enemies, so you want enemies to have Havoc Bane stacks from Yangyang or another team member before her hardest hitting attacks.
Her Resonance Liberation deals a large amount of Havoc damage, consumes all Melody, restores 1 Azure Plume, and powers up her next Sword Stance Flow with an extra follow-up attack.
Her gameplay rotation is as follows. Use Yangyang’s Resonance Liberation to gain one Azure Plume. Use Basic Attacks to deplete Melody, use Resonance Skill Flow to swap stances and gain the second Azure Plume, then cash out with her enhanced Heavy Attack.
If you intro into Yangyang and use her Resonance Liberation, she will immediately be able to cast her Enhanced Heavy Attack.

1413.name: Qingxiao
1413.synopsis:
Qingxiao is an Aero, Sword wielding character whom is a Tune Strain main DPS. Qingxiao's gameplay revolves around managing two Forte Gauges: Qin Heart and Sword Cadence.
Once both are full, she can use Heavy Attack - Stringblade to enter Ephemeral Transcendence. While in this state, her attacks generate Heart Sword Intent, which eventually allows her to unleash her powerful enhanced Heavy Attack, Heaven's Reckoning.
1413.rotationNotes:
A strong Qingxiao rotation starts with Intro Skill → Resonance Skill, giving her 30 Sword Cadence while Resonant Chime allows Severing Note Judgement to generate an additional 30 Qin Heart on top of its normal 45. Continue using Basic Attacks and Severing Note - Ascendant until Qin Heart and Sword Cadence are full, then hold Basic Attack for Heavy Attack - Stringblade.
During Ephemeral Transcendence, use enhanced Basic Attacks or Dodge Counters until Heart Sword Intent reaches 100, then hold Basic Attack to cast Heaven’s Reckoning. Avoid switching characters between Stringblade and Heaven’s Reckoning, as doing so removes Heaven’s Clarity’s enhancement to the finisher.
After Heaven’s Reckoning, use Resonance Liberation to take advantage of the Mindlock stacks built on the enemy and reapply Heaven’s Clarity, allowing Qingxiao to generate Qin Heart and Sword Cadence faster for her next rotation.
Sample Rotation:
Intro → Resonance Skill → Basics/Ascendant → Stringblade → Ephemeral Basics → Heaven’s Reckoning → Resonance Liberation → Repeat

Qingxiao's gameplay revolves around using her Basic Attacks and Resonance Skill together to quickly build Qin Heart and Sword Cadence. Her Resonance Skill: Severing Note Judgement is especially important, instantly granting 45 Qin Heart and allowing her to follow directly into Basic Attack Stage 4. If used after her Intro Skill, Resonant Chime grants an additional 30 Qin Heart.
Once Qin Heart and Sword Cadence both reach 100, hold Basic Attack to cast Heavy Attack - Stringblade, consuming both gauges and entering Ephemeral Transcendence. You will then cast her enhanced Basic Attacks or Dodge Counters to build Heart Sword Intent. Once Heart Sword Intent reaches 100, hold Basic Attack again to unleash Heaven's Reckoning, her heavy attack main finisher, before restarting the gauge-building process.
Each time a Resonator inflicts Tune Strain - Interfered, the enemy gains one stack of Mindlock, up to 15. Mindlock significantly increases the damage of Qingxiao's major attacks, granting additional damage amplification for every stack accumulated.
Qingxiao gains Heaven's Clarity upon entering combat or casting Resonance Liberation. Because Heaven's Reckoning removes Heaven's Clarity, you generally want to cast Resonance Liberation after her Forte finisher. This allows her Liberation to benefit from the Mindlock stacks built during the rotation while also reapplying Heaven’s Clarity for faster Forte generation during the next rotation.
